issues.description: New command names break the singular quickmark-/bookmark- convention used by every sibling command.
issues.detail: Existing commands are quickmark-save, quickmark-add, bookmark-add, bookmark-load (singular, hyphenated). The patch adds quickmarks-reload and bookmarks-reload (plural), and the feature file uses the plural form too. Rename to quickmark-reload / bookmark-reload to match the established vocabulary in the same file.

issues.description: reload() is not atomic: a parse error leaves marks empty rather than preserving prior state.
issues.detail: reload() calls self.marks.clear() and then re-parses. If _init_lineparser or _parse_line raises, marks is left half-populated or empty while the file on disk is intact, breaking the postcondition that marks matches disk or is unchanged. Build the new OrderedDict in a local, then swap on success and emit once.

issues.description: Routing __init__ through reload() now emits changed during construction, altering the signal's contract.
issues.detail: Previously __init__ populated marks without emitting changed. After the refactor, construction fires changed before _init_savemanager runs, which can mark the manager dirty and provoke an autosave round-trip of just-loaded data. Either suppress the signal during construction or document the new constructor postcondition.

issues.description: New BDD scenarios are unnamed and only assert the info message, not the actual reload behavior.
issues.detail: Both new Scenario: blocks lack titles, breaking the feature file's voice, and assert only that a message string appears. They do not mutate the file between writes and verify that marks were replaced. Name the scenarios and assert the resulting marks state to test what the command is about.

issues.description: Unit test coverage is thin: no removal/addition semantics, no QuickmarkManager path, no malformed-file case.
issues.detail: test_reload only verifies one entry replaced by another on BookmarkManager. It does not assert that entries removed from disk disappear, that QuickmarkManager (which overrides _parse_line) reloads correctly, or that a malformed file leaves prior state intact. Add tests for the disjoint-set, quickmark, and failure cases.

issues.description: reload() docstring omits pre/postconditions and the discard-unsaved-state contract.
issues.detail: The one-line docstring does not state the postcondition (marks equals on-disk contents; changed emitted once), the failure mode, or that any unflushed in-memory changes are silently discarded. State the supertype contract so subtypes inherit it and the next maintainer doesn't have to read the code.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, well-shaped refactor — folding __init__'s parse loop into a reusable reload() is the right move and should land. However, three substantive issues block merge: the new command names break the singular quickmark-/bookmark- convention used everywhere else in the file (unanimous), reload() is not atomic and leaves marks empty on parse failure (4 of 6), and routing __init__ through reload() silently changes the constructor's signal contract by emitting changed during construction. Tests are thin — both the unit test and the unnamed BDD scenarios verify surface behavior rather than the actual reload contract, missing the quickmark path, removal semantics, and the failure case. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — fix naming, parse-then-swap atomically, tighten the docstring contract, and expand test coverage before merging.
